purpose: Fix the persistently failing en-US-DavisNeural (NLV) voice in chapter audio generation, and make chapter failures impossible to miss silently again (run must fail loudly, partial progress preserved, failures retried on re-run).

Please verify that your parameters are correct.' after 3 retries.
current_failure_state_verified_from_live.scope: EVERY chapter of NLV (1,189) and VOICE (1,189) fails, 100% consistently across every recent run. The other 10 versions' voices all succeed (their audio is already committed; only NLV+VOICE remained).
current_failure_state_verified_from_live.why_silent: generate_audio.py catches per-chapter exceptions, prints 'FAILED <label>', and cmd_generate returns 0 regardless of failed count, so the Actions step exits 0 and the run is marked 'success'. Nothing aggregated the failures or turned them into a job failure, so this went unnoticed for days.

diagnosis.method: Live verification in sandbox with edge-tts 7.2.8 (same version the workflow installed in the failing runs).
findings: edge-tts version is NOT the problem: the failing runs installed edge-tts-7.2.8, and 7.2.8 reproduces the exact failure locally while other voices succeed on the same install.
Live voice catalog (edge_tts.list_voices(), 322 voices): en-US-DavisNeural and en-US-NancyNeural are BOTH MISSING. All 10 other assigned voices are PRESENT.

Live synthesis test (independent network, not GitHub runners): en-US-DavisNeural and en-US-NancyNeural both fail with the identical 'NoAudioReceived: No audio was received' error. en-US-AndrewNeural, en-US-ChristopherNeural, en-US-SteffanNeural, en-US-EmmaNeural succeed on the same network/install.

Broader retirement confirmed: other formerly-popular en-US voices (Ashley, Cora, Amber, Jane, Elizabeth, Brandon) are ALSO missing from the live catalog and also fail with the same error. Microsoft retired an entire batch of Read-Aloud voices. This is a permanent backend retirement, not throttling or a transient outage.

Root cause: Microsoft silently retired en-US-DavisNeural (and en-US-NancyNeural) from the Edge Read-Aloud backend. They no longer exist in the served voice list, so every synthesis request returns no audio. The correct fix is a replacement voice, not a dependency/parameter change.

VOICE.note: The operator-facing bug report named only DavisNeural; live-log inspection revealed NancyNeural (VOICE) failing identically, so both are fixed. en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural / en-US-EmmaMultilingualNeural also exist; single-locale EmmaNeural chosen to match the other single-locale narrators.

failure_signaling_fix.script_change: generate_audio.py now writes an aggregated AUDIO_FAILURE_SUMMARY block (and --summary-file JSON) listing every failed version/book/chapter + reason, and cmd_generate returns exit code 1 whenever failed>0 (while still committing every success first, preserving partial progress).
failure_signaling_fix.workflow_change: generate-audio.yml captures the generator's exit code, always runs the re-count, appends the failure summary to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (visible on the run page without opening raw logs), and the final step exits non-zero when the run had failures OR chapters remain unfinished — so the run is honestly marked FAILED instead of 'success'.
failure_signaling_fix.failure_tracking: Idempotency is unchanged and IS the failure tracking: resume state = the git tree (skip-if-.m4a-exists). Failed chapters never produce a committed .m4a, so any re-run (manual or auto-resume) retries exactly the previously-failed chapters and skips everything already generated. No blind re-rendering of finished chapters.
